scenes.heading: Idempotency & Safe Reruns
scenes.subheading: Run it twice, get the same result
scenes.narration: Idempotency means a pipeline can run twice on the same input and produce the same result, which is what makes reruns safe.

scenes.heading: Why idempotency is essential
bullets: Failures force reruns, and reruns must not duplicate data
Retries and backfills replay the same partitions
At-least-once delivery means messages arrive twice
Safe reruns let on-call recover without fear
scenes.narration: Failures are inevitable, and every rerun must avoid duplicating data. Retries and backfills routinely replay the same partitions, so operations have to be repeatable. Most streaming systems only guarantee at-least-once delivery, meaning duplicates will arrive. Idempotency lets an on-call engineer rerun a job at three in the morning without fear of corrupting the warehouse.

scenes.heading: Append vs idempotent write
scenes.narration: A naive append doubles rows every time you rerun, so duplicates pile up silently. An idempotent write instead overwrites the target partition or merges on a key, so the state always converges to the correct value. The difference is whether a rerun is a routine recovery or a data-quality incident.

scenes.heading: Idempotent merge on a key
scenes.code:
-- Rerunning this MERGE never creates duplicates
MERGE INTO orders_target t
USING orders_staging s
  ON t.order_id = s.order_id
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET
  t.status = s.status,
  t.amount = s.amount,
  t.updated_at = s.updated_at
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT
  (order_id, status, amount, updated_at)
  VALUES (s.order_id, s.status, s.amount, s.updated_at);
scenes.narration: This merge keys on the order identifier, updating a row when it already exists and inserting it only when it does not. Because the outcome depends solely on the input, running it once or ten times yields the same table. That property is exactly what makes the operation safe to retry.

scenes.heading: Patterns for idempotency
scenes.narration: The common patterns start with deterministic keys so the same input always maps to the same target. Overwriting an entire partition replaces rather than appends. Merging or upserting on a key handles record-level updates, and idempotency tokens let you deduplicate events that were delivered more than once.

scenes.text: Design every job so a rerun is a no-op when nothing changed. Idempotency is the foundation of stress-free recovery.
scenes.narration: Design every job so that rerunning it changes nothing when the input has not changed, because idempotency is the foundation of stress-free recovery.
